_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::membrane#1, and a correction to its recipe. The entry said to stabilise a membrane 'via PRESTRESS section or internal pressure DESIGN SURF NEUMANN'. On a FLAT sheet neither works: the same 4x4 MEMBRANE4 patch with orthopressure and no edge drive dies with 'Signal: Floating point exception (8)' after zero steps, and adding STRUCTURAL DYNAMIC PRESTRESS: 'MULF' changes nothing — it dies identically. Both are loads, and neither puts stress into the reference configuration, so the out-of-plane block of the tangent stays empty. Stretching the edges of the identical mesh by 10% runs all four steps and exits 0. The upstream membrane_cyl_new_struc deck shows the other half: on a CURVED surface orthopressure alone drives all ten steps, because there the pressure does generate in-plane stress. The stabiliser is in-plane stress, not the pressure or the PRESTRESS keyword as such. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: give the pressure-only arm the in-plane stretch it lacks. It then solves, EXIT_PRESSURE_ONLY becomes 0 and PRESSURE_ONLY_STEPS stops being 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the MULF arm the same way. EXIT_PRESTRESS_MULF becomes 0 and its floating-point exception disappears, so the fixture must go red.

remove the control: take the in-plane tension away from the third arm. It then dies like the first two, EXIT_INPLANE_TENSION stops being 0 and the fixture loses the contrast that carries the correction, so it must go red.
